title: Chamier: sins remitted before we believe — yet that faith does not justify
source_text: LXX. Chamierus autem simpliciter concedit peccata nobis esse remissa antequam credamus, & fidem justificatione posteriorem esse. Fidem tamen qua credimus peccata nobis jam esse remissa non justificare, quia efficitur in justificato, & requiritur a justificato; adeo ut nemo, qui quidem fruatur usu rationis, justificatus sit, nisi qui habeat hanc fidem, neque ullus habeat hanc fidem qui non sit justificatus. Panstratiae Catholicae. lib. 13. cap. 6.
pass_a_gloss: But Chamier simply grants that sins have been remitted to us before we believe, and that faith is later than justification. Yet that the faith by which we believe that sins have already been remitted to us does not justify, because it is wrought in the justified man, and is required of the justified man; so that no one who indeed enjoys the use of reason is justified unless he has this faith, nor does anyone have this faith who is not justified. Catholic Panstratia, book 13, chapter 6.
pass_b_english: Chamier: sins remitted to us before we believe; faith later than justification.
Yet the faith that sins are already remitted does not justify — it is wrought in, and required of, the already-justified.
No one of sound reason is justified without this faith; no one has this faith who is not justified.
